item.title: Fun with Slime
item.content:encoded:
Could SCP-294 dispense slime secretions from any other SCP (such as SCP-035, SCP-106, and SCP-447)? More pertinently, would this be a good idea (or at least not an instantly-suicidal idea; drinking 035 or 106's juice is an obvious death wish), or would the mere act of dispensing the slime have a high probability of resulting in structural damage to the facility (up to a possible containment breach) and/or SCP-447 coming into contact with a dead body?

Also, I had a funny idea where some newbie tries to use SCP-294 to exasanguinate SCP-682 by repeatedly ordering a cup of SCP-682 blood. Obviously, the machine would stop dispensing liquid before 682 even ended up being mildly lightheaded, but I'm wondering how long everyone else would humor the noob trying this. Or what sort of catastrophe might result from spreading 682's blood around willy-nilly.

item.title: Re: A way to receive diamonds
item.content:encoded:
If Dr. King asked for black coffee, he would end up with apple seeds; and if someone else asked for the superconductor, they would not get juice with seeds.

Because Dr. King is a meta-anomaly, his presence alters the function of other anomalies. Specifically, if he is involved there will always be apple seeds.

item.title: A way to receive diamonds
item.content:encoded:
Just another random thought here, maybe someone already had the same idea.
So SCP-294 does not dispense solid objects that do not exist in liquid state, such as diamonds.
However, in one of the tests we read that:
"Dr. King produced request for "a cup of room-temperature superconductor", and received a cup of apple juice with seeds floating in it."
Seeds are solid.
So that would mean SCP-294 is able to dispense solid objects only if they're mixed with the liquid.
Maybe instead of asking for diamonds, we should type in "cup of diamonds" or "water with diamonds".
or diamond juice

item.title: Re: Potential uses for Conservation
item.content:encoded:
While it is not the job of the foundation to help with conservation of mundane animals, I feel that maybe in this case an exception should be made?

I doubt it—not only would it take a lot of time and resources to process all the samples, the Foundation would also need to house and eventually relocate all the populations being saved.

It's an interesting thing to think about, but I don't see the Foundation doing that unless there's some sort of straightforward gain for them. Maybe if they sold the animals to collectors to build up funds, but that seems like a pretty roundabout and not super reliable (security and safety liabilities) way to attempt to make up for the resources lost.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Keter class is the only object class that has any coloration between containment breaches. Object classes have less to do with how hard it is to keep it contained and more with what it will do while it is contained. Euclid just means that what it will do is not guaranteed, as it is at least a little unpredictable in nature.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I thought it went like this:

Safe: Lock it up and we never have to worry about it breaching containment

Euclid: keep an eye on it and give it some extensive procedures and containment breaches shouldn't be often.

Keter: Breaches are gonna happen a lot no matter whatever the hell we do with it, or it's currently uncontainable. And it needs super high quality containment in order to keep it contained.

Let's see…12 ounce cup, call it 350 ml.
Density of water is 1 g/ml, so 350 grams of anti-water.
e=mc2, times two because an equal mass of plain matter would also be instantly converted to energy…so if successful test J would have produced an explosion of roughly 63 PetaJoules; or 15 megatons.

That's the same as the bomb dropped on Hiroshima, and someone let them try this in the break room?

I think it's clear that not only is 294 sentient; it's notably smarter than local staff!
